transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi doctor, I'm George. I'm here because when I get going, I tear through a ton of food really fast, way faster than I ever used to. It's really gotten to the point where it feels like my eating is getting out of hand.
When you're eating this way, do you feel like you're unable to stop or control how much you're eating, even if you want to?

Yes, absolutely. Once I start, it feels like a switch flips and I'm just shoveling food in on autopilot. Even while I'm telling myself, "George, stop, you're done," my hands keep going back to the pan like I'm not the one in charge.
How often do you experience these episodes of eating rapidly and feeling like you're unable to stop, and do you typically feel guilty or distressed afterwards?

This happens at least once or twice every week, usually late at night after everyone else has gone to bed. Afterwards, I just sit alone in the kitchen staring at the empty plates, hating myself and worrying that I'm completely ruining my health and my marriage.
During these episodes, do you typically eat alone, and do you consume a large amount of food in a short period, such as within 2 hours?

Yes, I almost always eat alone, usually standing in the kitchen late at night after my wife has gone to sleep. And it is a massive amount of food—I can polish off a whole spread of wings and sliders in just ten or fifteen minutes, which is way under two hours.
Do you also experience episodes where you eat a normal or small amount of food, but then try to compensate for it by purging, using laxatives, or excessively exercising to prevent weight gain?
No, I don't do anything like that at all. I've never tried to make myself throw up, use laxatives, or do intense workouts to make up for what I've eaten.
Can you tell me more about what typically triggers these episodes of rapid eating, such as emotional states or specific situations?

It usually happens when I'm feeling lonely, stressed, or wound up about money, especially after my wife and I argue about our finances. Ever since I stepped back from my event-planning work, I've had this huge void and lack of structure in my life, which often leads me to the kitchen late at night.
Can you estimate how many times a month you have these episodes of rapid eating, and do they always occur at night or can they happen at any time of day?

Since it happens about once or twice a week, that works out to around four to eight times a month. And yes, it almost always happens late at night after everyone else has gone to bed and the house is quiet.
Do you experience any significant weight fluctuations or concerns about your weight between these episodes of rapid eating?

Yes, I've gained a lot of weight very quickly, which has left me feeling sluggish and deeply embarrassed about my appearance. My primary care doctor even raised concerns about this rapid weight gain and my rising blood pressure. It's gotten so bad that I've been avoiding church and social events because I'm so self-conscious about my body now.
Have you noticed any significant emotional distress or impairment in your daily life due to these episodes of rapid eating and subsequent weight gain?

Yes, the emotional toll is huge—afterwards I'm filled with self-hatred and constantly worry that I'm ruining my health and my marriage. It's also completely disrupted my daily life because I've stopped taking on event-planning gigs and even avoid church gatherings. I'm just too embarrassed about my weight and terrified that I'll lose control around the food there.

Have you experienced any episodes of eating a large amount of food in a short period, feeling a lack of control during the episode, and experiencing guilt or distress afterwards, without using any methods to compensate for the calories consumed?

Yes, that describes my experience perfectly. I will cook enough wings and mac and cheese for a whole church potluck and then just polish it off on autopilot, completely unable to stop myself. Afterwards, I don't purge or do anything to compensate; I just sit there too stuffed to move, staring at the dirty pans and feeling intense self-hatred.
Can you describe the duration of these episodes of rapid eating, from the moment you start eating until you finally feel like you've stopped, and has this duration changed over time?

The actual eating happens incredibly fast, typically lasting only about 10 to 15 minutes before I look down and realize a massive amount of food is gone. The speed of these episodes hasn't really changed over time; it has felt just as rapid and out-of-control since this pattern first started about a year ago.

Can you confirm that these episodes of rapid eating, where you feel a lack of control and consume a large amount of food in a short time, such as within 2 hours, occur at least once a week for the past 3 months?

Yes, I can absolutely confirm that. For the past few months, it has been happening at least once or twice every week, usually late at night. Honestly, this whole pattern started over a year ago after I stepped back from my event work, so it's been going on much longer than three months.
